title: BlackRock’s Wei Li Prefers US Equities to Government Bonds

title: US 30-Year Bond Enters September on Worst Stretch Since 2006
summary: Not since 2006 have yields on the longest-maturity Treasuries been this high for this long, with a gaping budget deficit, another wave of corporate issuance and a potentially decisive Federal Reserve meeting set to keep investors wary of US debt in coming weeks.

title: El Niño and Disease Threaten West Africa’s Cocoa Harvest Again
summary: Simon Essah walks through his cocoa farm in southwest Ghana, pointing to trees scarred by black pod disease, the latest in a series of threats plaguing his crop this year.

title: US Stocks Fall as Yields Climb on Rate Hike Bets: Markets Wrap

title: Gold Extends Drop as Fresh Mideast Tensions Raise Fed Hike Bets
summary: Gold fell to the lowest in almost two weeks as fresh hostilities in the Middle East sent oil higher, adding to pressure on the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates.

title: Pakistan Backs US-Iran Peace Framework as Best Hope for Region
summary: Pakistan “firmly believes” the US-Iran peace framework that it helped broker in Islamabad offers the best prospect for peace in the region, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation on Tuesday.

title: Elliott Is Said to Take Stake in Air Liquide
summary: Elliott Investment Management has taken a stake in Air Liquide, pushing the industrial gas supplier to improve margins, according to people familiar with the matter. Representatives for Air Liquide and Elliott declined to comment. Bloomberg's Ben Scent explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Tells Carmakers to Keep Price War Away From Export Markets
summary: China told its carmakers to keep their cutthroat competitive actions, like steep price cuts, away from overseas markets as manufacturers increasingly look abroad for growth to counter a domestic slowdown.

title: NIB CEO Says Defense Project Pipeline Has Increased Rapidly
summary: Nordic Investment Bank Chief Executive Officer André Küüsvek speaks on Bloomberg Television as the Helsinki-based multilateral lender owned by the five Nordic and three Baltic countries formally added resilience, security and defense into its strategy. "We are in discussions with around 30 other potential borrowers and counterparts with a gross pipeline of about €1.2 billion worth of projects today on the table," Küüsvek says. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hyundai Monthly Sales Tumble to Four-Year Low on Labor Strikes
summary: Hyundai Motor Co. reported its lowest monthly sales in four years after labor strikes idled production in South Korea.

title: Russian Steel Demand Revives as War Damage Drives Construction
summary: Russian steelmakers are seeing signs of a recovery in domestic demand and prices as delayed construction projects resume and repairs to assets damaged by Ukrainian attacks help drive a revival.

title: Bessent Ramps Up Pressure on BOJ to Raise Interest Rates Further
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stepped up his increasingly public pressure on Japan to raise interest rates as the yen continued to weaken and the nation’s 10-year bond yield touched 3% for the first time since 1996.

title: Hormuz Hostilities Pick Up as Two Tankers Reportedly Struck
summary: Two oil supertankers attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz were struck late Monday by projectiles in quick succession, maritime security consultant Marisks said, the latest sign of renewed hostilities around the critical waterway.

title: Gilts Lead Global Bond Selloff as Traders Play Catch Up

title: Zinc Climbs to Highest in More Than Four Years on Supply Squeeze
summary: Zinc advanced to the highest level in more than four years on signs of tightening supply, building on a months-long rally.

title: Bond Slide Grips Emerging Markets as Fed Risk Drags Sentiment
summary: A global bond selloff spread to emerging markets as prospects for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month overshadowed the conflict in Iran and volatility tied to artificial intelligence as the main driver of sentiment.

title: Taiwan Fines Cathay SITE, Restricts Offshore Trust Offerings
summary: Cathay Securities Investment Trust, the asset-management arm of Taiwan’s largest financial conglomerate, is barred from applying to launch offshore securities investment trust funds for one year, after a former director’s outside role breached conflict-of-interest rules.

title: South African Factory Mood Sours as Production Momentum Slows
summary: South African manufacturing sentiment deteriorated as a slowdown in production momentum weighed on output and local demand came under pressure.

title: Shein’s Debut Shows the Cost of IPO Missing Its Growth Peak
summary: Shein Global Holdings Ltd.’s shares long-awaited market debut has come at an awkward time: the fast-fashion retailer’s peak growth years are behind it just as tariffs, regulatory pressure and intensifying competition are making its next phase harder.
